title: Design: Convert to Billable window shows its body and buttons
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin (a user with every setting, See Financial Data included).
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 pixels wide at 100% zoom.
  • Have Internal Work Orders turned on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have a regular customer (not flagged), with one asset.
  • Have a new work order for the regular customer, with one labor line (1.0 h) and one stock part with a cost, converted to No Charge with the category Goodwill, made for this test.
  • Open the attached pictures iwo-flow2-06-3b-convert-to-billable-confirm.png, iwo-happy-26-26-convert-to-billable.png at 100% zoom beside the screen.
custom_steps:
1. Open the no-charge work order.
  2. Click the three-dots menu in the header.
  3. Click Convert to Billable.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The work order opens.

Step 2:

  • The menu offers "Change category" and "Convert to Billable".

Step 3:

  • A window "Convert work order [number] to billable?" opens with the body "Every line is priced as a new line would be today. You can convert it to no charge again until it is invoiced."
  • Buttons Cancel then "Convert to Billable".

Words in square brackets in a message stand for the value they name, such as the work order's number or the customer's name exactly as it is saved; every other word of the message must match exactly.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close)

  • S2-R6: “On a no-charge work order the menu offers "Change category" and "Convert to Billable" until the work order is closed. Convert to Billable opens "Convert work order [number] to billable?" with the body "Every line is priced as a new line would be today. You can convert it to no charge again until it is invoiced." and the buttons Cancel and "Convert to Billable"; confirming removes the badge and the category and prices every line the way a new line on this work order would be priced that day: labor at the customer's labor rate, else the location's; parts from the pricing rules applied to the cost already on the line (the cost Close would post), not today's catalogue cost. Change category opens the dialog "Change category for work order [number]" with the Category select (the current category preselected) and, when the new category requires it, the Original work order and Original line selects of S2-R2 (changing to a category that does not require them clears them) and the buttons Cancel and Save; Save is enabled once the category, the original work order or the original line differs from the current values (as on a line, S12-R5), so a missing original can be added before Close; it changes nothing else. It is offered while the setting is off too (S2-N1). After Close the category is locked with the classification (S2-R9); a wrong category on a closed work order is fixed by Reopen, Change category and Close again, an accepted cost of one lock for everything. Cancelling or dismissing any of these leaves the work order as it was. If a no-charge estimate was sent to the portal, after Convert to Billable the portal hides the NO CHARGE stamp and shows the live price summary; Approve and Decline keep working and the advisor re-sends when wanted.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
